To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the main barriers to HIV testing in older adults were clinicians’ preconception of older people and low perceived risk, while the main facilitators to testing were regular use of health care services and being offered/encourage to test by a health care provider.

the main barriers to testing were clinicians’ preconception of older people as not being at risk and the main facilitators were regular contact with the healthcare services and being offered/encouarged to test by a clinician.

there are many potential barriers to testing for HIV in older patients, including clinicians' preconceptions that they are at low risk, but that regular use of healthcare, and being encouraged to test by a clinician, are important facilitators to testing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an intervention that will increase HIV testing rates in older people.
the identification of barriers and facilitators to testing for HIV in people over the age of 50 years.
the barriers and facilitators for HIV testing among people aged 50 and above.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no barriers to HIV testing in older people.
the most significant barrier to testing is clinicians’ preconceived ideas of older people and that the most significant facilitator is being offered testing by a clinician.
clinicians should encourage all patients aged ≥50 years who have risk factors for HIV to test, regardless of their perceived risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

clinicians need to be aware of the importance of offering HIV testing to all people aged 50 and above, and that they need to do so in an open, non-judgemental manner, and to be aware of their own preconceptions about this group.
clinicians need to be aware of the risk of late diagnosis among older people, be aware that they can be at risk of acquiring HIV and be aware that older people can have an active sex life.
clinicians’ preconceived beliefs about older patients may be the most important barrier to HIV testing in this age group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clinicians’ preconception about older people is a major barrier to HIV testing in this group, which needs to be addressed.
there are unique factors associated with testing among people aged 50 years and older that should be considered in the design of testing interventions for this population.
clinicians should not assume that older patients are less likely to have HIV.
